setup: 40 randomized boards never used for training (layout, wire stiffness, friction, slack and wire shape all vary), 3 forks each: 119 routing trials.

headline.label: Full system
headline.detail: GR00T first; force-controlled seating when it gets stuck at the snap-in; the expert retries an attempt that fails.

headline.label: GR00T + force-controlled seating
headline.detail: GR00T N1.7 reaches, grasps and carries the wire over the clip; a force-controlled routine finishes the snap-in when GR00T gets stuck.

headline.label: Builds Nemotron completed
headline.detail: Ten randomized boards built four ways: undisturbed, a wire pulled out of a fork, a connector slipping out of the fingers, both. Nemotron noticed every disturbance, re-planned and finished all 40, and its verdict always matched the simulator (expert routing; hand-written rules: 37).

training: NVIDIA Isaac GR00T N1.7, a 3-billion-parameter vision-language-action model
Two camera views (scene and wrist), the robot's 79-number state, and the instruction, e.g. "route the wire into fork F2"
The next 16 motions of the tool and gripper, 20 per second
About 2,700 episodes: force-guided expert demonstrations with recovery pushes, 228 DAgger takeovers from GR00T's own stuck states, and seat recoveries
Fine-tuned on Nebius AI Cloud, 1x NVIDIA L40S, 20,000 steps at batch 32 (about 4.5 hours per round)
NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory decides every step and checks the result
next: Further training (more DAgger rounds, a dedicated snap-in skill) can raise how much of the work GR00T does on its own.
